subject: Clarifying accounting retention vs customer data erasure request
messages:

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Data erasure request — invoices & usage records question

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking this — our legal team sent a data subject erasure request for one former engineer and they asked whether that covers billing records tied to their account. The request attached the standard DSR form.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can redact or delete line-item usage records (token-level logs) that were used to generate invoices, or whether we (Acme) are required to retain those for accounting/AML purposes? Our accounting team copied me on the mail (accounting@acme-analytics.com). We want to comply with the DSR but also ensure we don't break audit trails for our financials.

Attachments: [Attachment: Acme_DSR_Form.pdf (application/pdf)]

claire@acme-analytics.com
From: priyom_das@redwood.example.com <priyom_das@redwood.example.com>
To: Claire Ng <claire@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: accounting@acme-analytics.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data erasure request — invoices & usage records question

Claire —

Thanks for the clear note and the DSR form. Short answer: invoices and the billing ledger (the canonical invoice record we deliver) are treated as legal/accounting records and are retained per our finance retention policy; they are not deleted purely as a result of a typical DSR. However, there are important nuances for usage logs and token-level artifacts.

High-level policy points and practical steps:

- Invoice records (PDFs, invoice IDs, amounts, billing metadata) — retained for 7 years by default for our finance/audit obligations. Those records are the source of truth for accounts receivable and tax reporting; we cannot remove them on a DSR if retention is required by law or contractual obligations.

- Line-item usage logs / raw token traces — these are treated as operational telemetry. We keep aggregated usage and billing-ready summaries for invoicing and dispute resolution. For raw inputs/outputs tied to a specific user session we treat DSR requests as follows: if the record is exclusively personal data and no longer needed for a legitimate business purpose (including billing dispute resolution), we can delete or irreversibly pseudonymize it.

- When usage records are required to substantiate an invoice (billing disputes, chargebacks, compliance) we retain minimal provenance metadata (hashes, timestamps, aggregated token counts) rather than full request/response payloads. That lets us maintain an audit trail without keeping PII or full content.

- If you need a compliance exception (e.g., regulator requires preserving more granular logs) our finance team can flag an extended retention for those invoices. That is coordinated as a documented exception and surfaced in the customer contract.

Requested next steps from our side:
1) Please confirm whether Acme needs the raw line-by-line token traces for your internal audit or if aggregated billing summaries suffice.
2) If you want us to preserve additional artifacts for a specific invoice dispute, we can create an exception ticket (RC-5921) and retain the minimal necessary data.

I copied Lauren (Legal/Finance) to confirm the retention window and any contractual constraints. I also attached the relevant policy links.

Best,
Priyom
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.example.com

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com <lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data erasure request — invoices & usage records question

Claire, Priyom —

Quick legal confirmation from our side: Redwood must comply with lawful retention obligations (tax, accounting, anti-fraud). For US customers like Acme, standard practice is to retain invoice and ledger data for up to 7 years unless a different period is contractually agreed. Those records are not removed by a DSR where retention is required by law or where they are necessary for our legitimate interests (e.g., financial recordkeeping).

For clarity:
- We will not delete the invoice PDF or the line on the ledger that documents the charge.
- We can delete or redact any PII contained in operational logs (e.g., request payloads) once they are not needed for dispute resolution, unless you request otherwise.
- If you need a signed statement for auditors that the invoice will be preserved and what subset of telemetry is retained, we can provide a retention statement.

Aditya (finance) — can you confirm the exact ledger retention language and whether we should auto-flag any invoice rows tied to active DSRs for review?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com
From: aditya_rao@redwood.example.com <aditya_rao@redwood.example.com>
To: Claire Ng <claire@acme-analytics.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.example.com, priyom_das@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data erasure request — invoices & usage records question

Claire —

Confirming the finance position: Redwood retains invoices and the underlying billing ledger for 7 years by default (we can shorten/extend via contract amendment). For operational usage logs we keep aggregated billing summaries indefinitely for charge reconciliation; raw request payloads and token traces are purged per the customer-configurable data lifecycle (typical default 90 days) unless flagged for dispute.

Operational practice we propose for this DSR:
1) We will preserve Invoice-2026-11-ACME.pdf and ledger entries tied to that invoice and provide a signed retention note for your auditors.
2) We will evaluate the DSR target (the former engineer). If the data subject's personal identifiers appear only in raw request payloads (not on the invoice), we will schedule deletion of those payloads after a 7-day hold unless you ask us to hold longer for investigation.
3) If you want us to pseudonymize the payloads instead of deleting, we can replace any PII with deterministic hashes and keep the records for dispute traceability.

I've created support ticket RC-5921 and attached the invoice to the ticket for reference. If this plan works, reply and we'll execute the hold and provide the signed retention confirmation this week.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
